The stronger conclusion is true, but the reduction is omitted: local finiteness at 0 supplies a finite-mass ball B(0,R); place disjoint balls B((R/2)e_j,R/8) inside it, force their common mass to zero, and use a countable cover by balls of radius R/8. Include that reduction or otherwise justify the locally finite wording.

original_concerns.reason: Finiteness on every bounded Borel set is stronger than local finiteness on a non-locally-compact Hilbert space. Existing proof only establishes the stronger-premise case, whereas the title/final assertion excludes every locally finite reference. The proposed proof chooses a finite-mass ball B(0,R), packs disjoint r=R/8 balls centered at(R/2)e_j in it, obtains their common mass zero, and covers ell² by countably many radius-r balls using the existing explicit dense set. It proves the full claimed locally-finite conclusion with the same Gaussian witness and no new supplier.

required_own_edits.source_excerpt: 1.2 Suppose that $\lambda$ is a translation-invariant Borel measure finite on every bounded Borel set. Put $U_j=\{x:\|x-e_j\|_2<1/3\}$. For $j\ne k$, $\|e_j-e_k\|_2=\sqrt2>2/3$, so the $U_j$ are pairwise disjoint. Each lies in the bounded ball $\{x:\|x\|_2<2\}$ by the triangle inequality. Translation invariance gives $\lambda(U_j)=m$ independent of $j$. If $m>0$, the first $N$ disjoint balls have total measure $Nm$ for every $N$, contradicting finiteness of the radius-two ball. Hence $m=0$. [F2, given, algebra]
required_own_edits.proposed_replacement: 1.2 Suppose that $\lambda$ is a nonzero locally finite translation-invariant Borel measure, where locally finite means that every point has a neighborhood of finite measure. At zero choose $R>0$ with $\lambda(B(0,R))<\infty$. Put $r=R/8$ and $U_j=B((R/2)e_j,r)$. For $j\ne k$ the distance between the centers is $R/\sqrt2>2r$, so these balls are pairwise disjoint, and every $U_j$ lies in $B(0,R)$ because $R/2+r<R$. Translation invariance gives a common finite mass $m=\lambda(U_j)$. If $m>0$, finite additivity and monotonicity give $Nm\le\lambda(B(0,R))$ for every $N$, a contradiction. Hence $m=0$. This covers in particular every measure finite on all bounded Borel sets, since that condition implies local finiteness. [F2, F4, given, algebra]

required_own_edits.source_excerpt: 2.1 Translation invariance and step 1.2 make every radius-$1/3$ ball have measure zero. Let $D$ be the set of finitely supported rational sequences. [F3] makes $D$ countable: it is the countable union, over support lengths $N$, of the countable set $\mathbb Q^N$ padded with zeros. It is dense in $\ell^2$: for any $x\in\ell^2$ and $\epsilon>0$, choose $N$ so that the squared tail sum is less than $\epsilon^2/4$, then approximate the first $N$ coordinates by rationals with squared total error less than $\epsilon^2/4$; the resulting padded vector is within $\epsilon$ of $x$. The radius-$1/3$ balls centered at $D$ therefore form a countable cover of $\ell^2$. By [F2], $\lambda(\ell^2)=0$, and [F4] makes every Borel subset null. This contradicts that $\lambda$ is nonzero. Hence no such reference measure exists, refuting the statement; in particular, the displayed Gaussian has no density relative to one. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.2, given, algebra, choose] ∎
